$comment: TEMPLATE for dependency-graph.json. Produced by L1-planning-dependency-mapper (Core), evaluated by L1-planning-dependency-mapper-evaluator. Consumes impact-assessment.md + prd.md (prd.md composes requirements.md + nfr-spec.md — see prd.template.md). Consumed by L1-planning-backlog-prioritizer (topological-sort input) and L1-design-hld (Phase 4). This is a structural schema — it validates shape, not acyclicity. Acyclicity is a separate, mandatory check (gr-L1-output-schema-validator hard-fails and escalates to HITL on any detected cycle; this cannot be expressed as a JSON Schema constraint alone, so the mapper agent must run an explicit cycle-detection pass and report the result in cycle_check below).
title: DependencyGraph

type.description: component = new/existing system to be built; external-dependency = a real prerequisite outside the build (partner, vendor) — not the same as an org-internal existing system

source_requirement.description: All FR-NNN ids this node traces back to, if it's a component derived from impact-assessment.md. Use an array even for one FR — a node satisfying multiple requirements (e.g. one reporting component covering two metrics) must list all of them, not just the first.

type.description: Direction is UNIFORM across all three types: 'from' is always the upstream/prerequisite node and 'to' is always the downstream/dependent node — i.e. 'from' must exist/complete before 'to' can proceed. depends-on = hard technical prerequisite between two components (edge: prerequisite -> dependent, e.g. identity-verification-service -> verification-confidence-limit-engine, read as "verification-confidence-limit-engine depends on identity-verification-service" even though the arrow points the other way); blocks = an external-dependency node gating a component (edge: blocker -> blocked); integrates-with = non-blocking peer integration (edge: producer -> consumer; failure of 'to' does not halt 'from'). Do not mix directions within a type — every edge, regardless of type, follows prerequisite -> dependent so topological sort and critical-path traversal work with a single consistent forward walk.

cycles_found.description: empty array if status is PASS; each inner array is the node-id sequence forming a cycle if FAIL

nodes.description: ordered node ids forming the longest blocking (depends-on/blocks) chain — integrates-with edges are excluded since they're non-blocking
